d4af100e4e6d.content: World Health Organization (2023). Pandemic influenza preparedness framework: annual progress report, 1 January – 31 December 2022. World Health Organization. TitlePandemic influenza preparedness framework: annual progress report, 1 January – 31 December 2022 AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2023-8-4 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240076907 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThe Pandemic Influenza Preparedness (PIP) Framework: annual progress report, 1 January–31 December 2022 presents technical and financial progress in implementing the PIP Framework, which aims to strengthen the sharing of influenza viruses with human pandemic potential and improve developing countries’ access to pandemic vaccines and other response supplies. The report assesses progress under the High-Level Implementation Plan II (2018–2023), including activities financed through the industry-funded Partnership Contribution mechanism. The report documents achievements and challenges in influenza laboratory capacity and surveillance, virus sharing, disease burden estimation, regulatory preparedness, risk communication and community engagement, deployment planning, and national pandemic preparedness. In 2022, 91% of Partnership Contribution recipient countries reported influenza data to FluNet, 48 countries had implemented regulatory approaches for pandemic influenza products, and 37 countries had developed or updated pandemic preparedness plans. It also presents progress in securing pandemic response products through benefit-sharing agreements, alongside financial allocations, expenditures and implementation milestones. 0dc5b72e31f3.doc: Classification des interventions, des services et des applications numériques dans le domaine de la santé : un langag…
0dc5b72e31f3.title: Classification des interventions, des services et des applications numériques dans le domaine de la santé : un langag…
0dc5b72e31f3.content: Organisation mondiale de la Santé (2024). Classification des interventions, des services et des applications numériques dans le domaine de la santé : un langage commun pour décrire les diverses utilisations de la technologie numérique dans le domaine de la santé. Organisation mondiale de la Santé. TitleClassification des interventions, des services et des applications numériques dans le domaine de la santé : un langage commun pour décrire les diverses utilisations de la technologie numérique dans le domaine de la santé AuthorsOrganisation mondiale de la Santé Issued2024-9-12 Typebook PublisherOrganisation mondiale de la Santé ISBN9789240093720 (version électronique) Languagefr AbstractCette deuxième édition de la Classification des interventions, services et applications numériques en santé présente une taxonomie normalisée permettant de décrire la manière dont les technologies numériques sont utilisées pour répondre aux besoins des individus et des systèmes de santé. Élaborée par l’OMS, cette classification établit un langage commun destiné à faciliter la communication entre les décideurs, les responsables de programmes de santé, les chercheurs, les responsables de mise en œuvre, les développeurs de technologies et les autres acteurs du domaine de la santé numérique. Elle organise les interventions numériques en santé autour de capacités technologiques distinctes conçues pour répondre à des défis des systèmes de santé et relie ces interventions aux services et types d’applications numériques qui les mettent en œuvre. La publication met à jour et élargit la première édition publiée en 2018 afin de refléter les progrès des technologies de santé numérique, l’évolution des pratiques de mise en œuvre et les enseignements tirés de leur utilisation à l’échelle mondiale. Le cadre est structuré autour de trois axes interconnectés : les défis des systèmes de santé, les interventions numériques en santé et les services et types d’applications numériques. Il comprend des interventions destinées aux personnes, aux prestataires de soins, aux gestionnaires des systèmes de santé et aux services de données, ainsi que des catégories d’applications numériques et de systèmes d’information. Cette classification vise à soutenir la planification, la mise en œuvre, l’analyse des investissements, la recherche, l’interopérabilité, l’élaboration des politiques et la gouvernance des initiatives de santé numérique. 971ef94e62c6.content: World Health Organization (2020). WHO operational handbook on tuberculosis: module 1: prevention: tuberculosis preventive treatment. World Health Organization. TitleWHO operational handbook on tuberculosis: module 1: prevention: tuberculosis preventive treatment AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2020-3-23 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240002906 Languageen AbstractThis operational handbook provides practical guidance for the programmatic management and scale-up of tuberculosis preventive treatment (TPT) in line with WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis. The publication addresses the global burden of tuberculosis infection and the need to expand preventive interventions among populations at high risk of developing TB disease, particularly people living with HIV, household contacts of TB patients and other vulnerable groups. It supports implementation of commitments made at the United Nations High-Level Meeting on Tuberculosis and outlines strategies to strengthen national responses through integrated, people-centred approaches. The handbook describes the cascade of care for TPT, including identification of target populations, exclusion of active TB disease, testing for TB infection, treatment options, management of adverse events, adherence support, monitoring and evaluation, and ethical considerations. It also provides operational guidance for contact investigation, integration of preventive services with active TB case finding and HIV services, health system strengthening, and resource mobilization. Practical implementation tools, policy considerations and monitoring indicators are included to assist national TB programmes, policy-makers and health-care providers in adapting and scaling up TPT services in diverse epidemiological and health system settings. 0d6b6164c472.doc: Enumeration of CD4 T lymphocytes : report of a workshop, Bangkok, Thailand, 6-10 June 2006
0d6b6164c472.title: Enumeration of CD4 T lymphocytes : report of a workshop, Bangkok, Thailand, 6-10 June 2006
0d6b6164c472.content: World Health Organization. Regional Office for South-East Asia (2006). Enumeration of CD4 T lymphocytes : report of a workshop, Bangkok, Thailand, 6-10 June 2006. WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia. TitleEnumeration of CD4 T lymphocytes : report of a workshop, Bangkok, Thailand, 6-10 June 2006 AuthorsWorld Health Organization. Regional Office for South-East Asia Issued2006-12-31 Typedocument PublisherWHO Regional Office for South-East Asia Languageen AbstractDescription: Enumeration of CD4 T lymphocytes is essential for initiation of antiretroviral therapy for a person with HIV as well as for monitoring the response to treatment. The techniques for enumeration of CD4 T lymphocytes are evolving. The flow cytometry continues to be the gold standard of CD4 T lymphocytes enumeration in spite of the fact that the technology is expensive both in terms of initial investment in sophisticated equipment and running cost. The newer techniques may be economical to procure and maintain. The latter are particularly intended for countries with limited resources. WHO conducted a workshop to orient the nationals about these technologies and integration of a quality system into routine testing, at Siriraj Hospital Bangkok. The report describes the status of CD4 testing in these countries. While Indonesia, India and Thailand have developed a good infrastructure for enumeration of CD4 T lymphocytes, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Nepal and Sri Lanka have made a beginning in this direction. The workshop focussed on principles of various techniques and imparted a hands-on training for performing the same. The issues regarding selection of technology, procurement of equipment and their maintenance; ensuring continuous supply and economical use of reagents and biosafety in laboratory were discussed and have been presented in this Report. a617f8c7534b.content: World Health Organization (2023). Digital adaptation kit for HIV: operational requirements for implementing WHO recommendations in digital systems. World Health Organization. TitleDigital adaptation kit for HIV: operational requirements for implementing WHO recommendations in digital systems AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2023-12-21 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240085138 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis second edition of the digital adaptation kit for HIV provides operational, software-neutral requirements to support the incorporation of WHO clinical, public health and data use recommendations into digital systems. Developed within the SMART Guidelines approach, it focuses on the content requirements for person-centred digital tracking and decision support systems used by health workers for HIV services in primary health care settings. The kit is intended to facilitate transparent, consistent and adaptable translation of narrative guidance into digital implementations while supporting interoperability and local customization. The publication organizes HIV-related requirements into eight components: health interventions and associated recommendations; generic personas; illustrative user scenarios; business processes and workflows; core data elements; decision support and scheduling logic; indicators and performance metrics; and high-level functional and non-functional requirements. It covers processes including HIV testing, pre-exposure prophylaxis, care and treatment, prevention of mother-to-child transmission, infant diagnosis, diagnostics, client follow-up, referral, and aggregate reporting and data use, with complementary operational resources provided in web annexes. 4851e6f550bc.doc: WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 5: management of tuberculosis in children and adolescents
4851e6f550bc.title: WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 5: management of tuberculosis in children and adolescents
4851e6f550bc.content: World Health Organization (2022). WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 5: management of tuberculosis in children and adolescents. World Health Organization. TitleWHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 5: management of tuberculosis in children and adolescents AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2022-3-18 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240046764 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractTuberculosis (TB) remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality among children and adolescents, with substantial gaps in case detection, diagnosis and access to preventive treatment worldwide. This guideline consolidates new and existing WHO recommendations for the management of TB in these populations, replacing the 2014 guidance and reflecting the latest evidence on prevention, screening, diagnosis, treatment and models of care. It aims to support countries in strengthening the continuum of TB care and improving health outcomes through evidence-based policies and practices tailored to the specific needs of children, adolescents and their families. The publication provides recommendations on TB screening and contact investigation, TB preventive treatment, diagnostic approaches, treatment of drug-susceptible and drug-resistant TB, management of TB meningitis, and decentralized, family-centred models of care. It incorporates updated evidence on the use of Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra, integrated treatment decision algorithms, shortened treatment regimens for non-severe TB, and therapeutic options for multidrug- or rifampicin-resistant disease in children. Developed according to WHO guideline development standards, the document is intended for national TB programmes, policy-makers, health professionals and implementing partners, and contributes to global efforts to reduce TB-related morbidity and mortality in line with the End TB Strategy and Sustainable Development Goals. 1b1eabceaa3b.title: Consolidated HIV guidelines: service delivery
1b1eabceaa3b.content: World Health Organization (2026). Consolidated HIV guidelines: service delivery. World Health Organization. TitleConsolidated HIV guidelines: service delivery AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2026-7-22 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240124233 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractHIV remains a major public health challenge, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, despite the availability of effective treatment and prevention tools. Many evidence-based interventions are not implemented consistently or delivered in a timely manner, contributing to ongoing HIV transmission, advanced disease and preventable mortality. These consolidated WHO guidelines provide evidence-based recommendations to strengthen HIV service delivery through people-centred, integrated and equitable approaches that improve access to care, continuity of treatment and accelerate progress towards ending AIDS as a public health threat. The publication consolidates all WHO recommendations on HIV service delivery issued between 2013 and 2025. It is intended to support the development of national and subnational policies, clinical guidelines and implementation guidance. It addresses key components of HIV service delivery, including linkage to care and antiretroviral therapy initiation, clinical follow-up and medication refills, adherence support and re-engagement in care, services for adolescents and young people, task sharing, decentralized service delivery, and integration with maternal and child health, tuberculosis, sexual and reproductive health, diabetes, hypertension and mental health services. Recommendations are classified as new, updated or revalidated according to WHO guideline development procedures. 078a6327e364.title: Understanding national health workforce accounts
078a6327e364.content: World Health Organization (2017). Understanding national health workforce accounts. World Health Organization. TitleUnderstanding national health workforce accounts AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2017-12-31 Typereport PublisherWorld Health Organization Languageen AbstractUnderstanding National Health Workforce Accounts (NHWA) is an introductory guidance document developed by the World Health Organization to explain the purpose, policy relevance and structure of the National Health Workforce Accounts framework. The publication outlines how NHWA supports the standardization of health workforce information systems, improves the quality and comparability of data, and strengthens the evidence base for health workforce policy, planning and monitoring. Positioned within the context of universal health coverage, the Sustainable Development Goals, the Global Strategy on Human Resources for Health: Workforce 2030, and related international commitments, the document highlights the importance of reliable workforce information for addressing current and future health system challenges. The publication describes the benefits of NHWA at national, regional and global levels and presents key policy questions that can be informed through systematic workforce data collection and analysis. It introduces the health labour market framework used by NHWA, emphasizing workforce production, labour market flows, distribution, productivity and regulation. The document also summarizes the development process of the NHWA indicators and explains the modular structure of the framework, which comprises ten modules covering workforce stock, education, labour market dynamics, employment conditions, financing, governance, planning and information systems. Together, these elements provide a foundation for evidence-informed decision-making and strengthened health workforce monitoring. 39f0bc59c3e9.title: Cost-effectiveness of introducing the pneumococcal conjugate vaccine for children under 5 years in the Islamic Republ…
39f0bc59c3e9.content: Khadijeh Ezoji; Mohsen Yaghoubi; Marzieh Nojomi; et al. (2019). Cost-effectiveness of introducing the pneumococcal conjugate vaccine for children under 5 years in the Islamic Republic of Iran. World Health Organization. Regional Office for the Eastern Mediterranean. TitleCost-effectiveness of introducing the pneumococcal conjugate vaccine for children under 5 years in the Islamic Republic of Iran AuthorsKhadijeh Ezoji; Mohsen Yaghoubi; Marzieh Nojomi; Sussan Mahmoody; Seyed Mohsen Zahraie; Maziar Moradi-Lakeh; Sedigheh R. Tabatabaei; Abdollah Karimi Issued2019-10-29 Typedocument PublisherWorld Health Organization. Regional Office for the Eastern Mediterranean DOIhttps://doi.org/10.26719/emhj.19.039 Languageen AbstractBackground: Pneumococcal disease caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae results in considerable mortality and morbidity. Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCV), such as PCV-13, can prevent invasive pneumococcal disease and avoid disability and death. The cost of introducing PCV-13 in childhood immunization schedules should be assessed against the cost of pneumococcal diseases for each community. Aims: This study aimed to evaluate the cost–effectiveness of introducing PCV-13 in the national immunization programme for children under 5 years in the Islamic Republic of Iran. Methods: The TRIVAC decision support model was used to estimate total costs of introducing PCV-13 and the disability-adjusted life years (DALYs)averted. The main pneumococcal diseases were considered—pneumonia, meningitis, acute otitis media, and non-pneumonia, non-meningitis infections—in terms of hospital admissions, outpatient visits and deaths. Local data were used to estimate costs. Results: Pneumococcal disease is estimated to affect 18 713 211 children under 5 years (519 412 pneumonia, 18 148 116 acute otitis media, 6884 meningitis, and 38 799 non-pneumonia, non-meningitis)in 10 years (2014–2023)without use of the vaccine. Introduction of PCV-13 would prevent 4 900 084 cases of pneumococcal disease (190 849 pneumonia, 4 692 450 acute otitis media, 2529 meningitis, and 14 256 non-pneumonia, non-meningitis). Pneumococcal infection would cause 287 950 hospital admissions and 29 399 deaths; vaccination could avert 105 802 hospital admissions and 9997 deaths. The incremental cost–effectiveness was estimated to be US$ 1890 and US$ 1538 per averted DALY for the government and society respectively. Conclusion: According to WHO-recommended thresholds for interpreting cost–effectiveness, introduction of PCV-13 for children under 5 years in the Islamic Republic of Iran would be cost-effective Sources . | iris.who.int/handle/10665/385346 (canonical) | doi:https://doi.org/10.26719/emhj.19.039 (doi) | repository record (repository) | . 8a3274534c36.content: World Health Organization (2026). Digital transformation handbook for reporting substandard and falsified medical products. World Health Organization. TitleDigital transformation handbook for reporting substandard and falsified medical products AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2026-6-9 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240120747 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis handbook provides practical guidance to support countries in planning, designing and implementing digital solutions for reporting substandard and falsified medical products. These products pose a significant threat to public health, contributing to therapeutic failure, adverse effects, loss of trust in health systems and broader socioeconomic impacts. Effective detection and reporting are essential to enable regulatory authorities to investigate suspected cases, remove harmful products from circulation and contribute to global surveillance efforts through mechanisms such as WHO’s Global Surveillance and Monitoring System. The document outlines a structured approach to digital transformation, covering assessment of the current environment, stakeholder engagement, governance and policy alignment, definition of system requirements, implementation planning, and monitoring and evaluation. It emphasizes the transition from fragmented or paper-based reporting systems to interoperable digital platforms that improve data quality, standardization and timeliness. Drawing on global experience and existing WHO frameworks, the handbook promotes the use of user-centred design, open standards and integration with pharmacovigilance systems. It is intended for ministries of health, national regulatory authorities and partners seeking to strengthen reporting systems and enhance the capacity to detect and respond to substandard and falsified medical products. ec595f0a2a92.title: Consolidated guidelines on the use of antiretroviral drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection: recommendations…
ec595f0a2a92.content: World Health Organization (2016). Consolidated guidelines on the use of antiretroviral drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection: recommendations for a public health approach. World Health Organization. TitleConsolidated guidelines on the use of antiretroviral drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection: recommendations for a public health approach AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2016-6-6 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789241549684 Languageen AbstractThis evidence-based guideline consolidates World Health Organization recommendations on the use of antiretroviral (ARV) drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection, providing a comprehensive public health framework for HIV diagnosis, prevention, treatment, service delivery, and monitoring and evaluation across all age groups and populations. Developed in response to advances in scientific evidence and evolving programmatic needs, the second edition updates the 2013 consolidated guidelines and incorporates new recommendations, including universal eligibility for antiretroviral therapy (ART) regardless of CD4 cell count, expanded use of pre-exposure prophylaxis, and optimized approaches to HIV testing, treatment monitoring and management of coinfections and comorbidities. The guideline also outlines the methods used for guideline development and the principles underpinning a public health approach. The publication provides evidence-based recommendations on HIV testing services, antiretroviral therapy, prevention interventions, differentiated service delivery models, linkage to care, adherence, decentralization, task sharing, laboratory services and programme monitoring. It emphasizes integrated, people-centred and community-based approaches to improve access to high-quality HIV services, strengthen health systems and support implementation in diverse epidemiological settings. Intended primarily for national HIV programme managers, clinicians, policy-makers and implementing partners, the guideline aims to accelerate progress towards universal access to HIV services and the global goal of ending the HIV epidemic as a major public health threat by 2030. 354a7108bbaa.title: Global strategy on digital health 2020-2025
354a7108bbaa.content: World Health Organization (2021). Global strategy on digital health 2020-2025. World Health Organization. TitleGlobal strategy on digital health 2020-2025 AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2021-8-18 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240020924 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThe Global strategy on digital health 2020–2025 provides a framework to support Member States in strengthening health systems through the appropriate adoption and use of digital technologies. Developed in response to World Health Assembly mandates and aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals and WHO’s Triple Billion targets, the strategy outlines a shared vision for improving health and well-being through accessible, affordable, secure and sustainable digital health solutions. It emphasizes the importance of strong governance, interoperability, ethical use of data, privacy protection, workforce capacity-building and investment in digital infrastructure to support national health priorities and universal health coverage. The document establishes four strategic objectives: promoting global collaboration and knowledge exchange; advancing the implementation of national digital health strategies; strengthening governance for digital health at global, regional and national levels; and advocating people-centred health systems enabled by digital technologies. It also presents guiding principles, an implementation framework and monitoring mechanisms to support countries in developing interoperable digital health ecosystems. Particular attention is given to addressing barriers faced by low- and middle-income countries and ensuring that digital transformation contributes to equitable, effective and resilient health systems. TitleDigital adaptation kit for HIV: operational requirements for implementing: WHO recommendations in digital systems: web annex B: decision-support logic AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2023-12-14 Typereport PublisherWorld Health Organization Languageen AbstractThis web annex provides the standardized decision-support logic supporting the WHO Digital adaptation kit for HIV: operational requirements for implementing WHO recommendations in digital systems. It translates WHO HIV recommendations into structured, software-neutral decision tables that can be incorporated into digital tracking and decision-support systems to support consistent clinical and public health decision-making. The annex includes decision logic for HIV testing, prevention, treatment, advanced HIV disease, prevention of mother-to-child transmission, diagnostics, follow-up and related service delivery workflows, using standardized input expressions, decision rules, outputs, scheduling logic and triggering events. It also provides implementation guidance on rule syntax, comparison operators, hit policies and coding conventions to promote transparency, interoperability and consistent interpretation across digital platforms. Intended for software developers, digital health architects, implementers and programme managers, this resource supports the development and adaptation of standards-based decision-support functionality that accurately reflects WHO recommendations while allowing contextualization for national policies and health system requirements. 51051cf2d7c4.content: World Health Organization (2017). National health workforce accounts: a handbook. World Health Organization. TitleNational health workforce accounts: a handbook AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2017-10-26 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789241513111 Languageen AbstractThis handbook introduces the National Health Workforce Accounts (NHWA), a standardized framework developed by the World Health Organization to strengthen health workforce information systems and support evidence-based workforce planning and policy-making. The publication is intended to assist countries in monitoring and analysing health workforce capacity, distribution, education, labour market dynamics, financing, governance and information systems in the context of universal health coverage and the health-related Sustainable Development Goals. It outlines the rationale for improved health workforce data and highlights the role of harmonized metrics in addressing challenges related to workforce availability, accessibility, performance and retention. The handbook presents a modular framework comprising 78 core indicators organized across 10 modules covering active workforce stock, education and training, regulation and accreditation, education financing, labour market flows, employment conditions, workforce spending and remuneration, skill mix, governance, and health workforce information systems. For each indicator, it provides definitions, methodological guidance, reporting requirements, data sources and disaggregation options. The publication also describes implementation principles, reporting standards and potential applications of the NHWA, supporting countries in strengthening health workforce monitoring, facilitating international comparability and informing policies aimed at improving health system performance and population access to quality health services. f82596934847.doc: Stratégie mondiale pour la santé numérique 2020-2025
f82596934847.title: Stratégie mondiale pour la santé numérique 2020-2025
f82596934847.content: Organisation mondiale de la Santé (2021). Stratégie mondiale pour la santé numérique 2020-2025. Organisation mondiale de la Santé. TitleStratégie mondiale pour la santé numérique 2020-2025 AuthorsOrganisation mondiale de la Santé Issued2021-8-18 Typebook PublisherOrganisation mondiale de la Santé ISBN9789240027558 (version électronique) Languagefr AbstractLa Stratégie mondiale pour la santé numérique 2020–2025 fournit un cadre destiné à aider les États Membres à renforcer leurs systèmes de santé grâce à l’adoption et à l’utilisation appropriées des technologies numériques. Élaborée en réponse aux mandats de l’Assemblée mondiale de la Santé et alignée sur les Objectifs de développement durable ainsi que sur les objectifs du « Triple milliard » de l’OMS, cette stratégie présente une vision commune visant à améliorer la santé et le bien-être au moyen de solutions de santé numérique accessibles, abordables, sûres et durables. Elle souligne l’importance d’une gouvernance solide, de l’interopérabilité, de l’utilisation éthique des données, de la protection de la vie privée, du renforcement des capacités des personnels de santé et des investissements dans les infrastructures numériques afin de soutenir les priorités nationales de santé et la couverture sanitaire universelle. Le document définit quatre objectifs stratégiques : promouvoir la collaboration mondiale et le partage des connaissances ; faire progresser la mise en œuvre des stratégies nationales de santé numérique ; renforcer la gouvernance de la santé numérique aux niveaux mondial, régional et national ; et promouvoir des systèmes de santé centrés sur les personnes grâce aux technologies numériques. Il présente également des principes directeurs, un cadre de mise en œuvre et des mécanismes de suivi destinés à soutenir les pays dans le développement d’écosystèmes numériques interopérables. Une attention particulière est accordée aux obstacles rencontrés par les pays à revenu faible ou intermédiaire et à la nécessité de veiller à ce que la transformation numérique contribue à des systèmes de santé plus équitables, efficaces et résilients. 132b822c59b2.title: Clasificación de intervenciones, servicios y aplicaciones digitales en salud: un lenguaje compartido para describir l…
132b822c59b2.content: Organización Mundial de la Salud (2024). Clasificación de intervenciones, servicios y aplicaciones digitales en salud: un lenguaje compartido para describir los usos de la tecnología digital para la salud. Organización Mundial de la Salud. TitleClasificación de intervenciones, servicios y aplicaciones digitales en salud: un lenguaje compartido para describir los usos de la tecnología digital para la salud AuthorsOrganización Mundial de la Salud Issued2024-9-24 Typebook PublisherOrganización Mundial de la Salud ISBN9789240093744 (versión electrónica) Languagees AbstractEsta segunda edición de la Clasificación de intervenciones, servicios y aplicaciones digitales en salud proporciona una taxonomía normalizada para describir cómo se utilizan las tecnologías digitales para responder a las necesidades de las personas y de los sistemas de salud. Desarrollada por la OMS, la clasificación establece un lenguaje común destinado a facilitar la comunicación entre responsables de la formulación de políticas, gestores de programas de salud, investigadores, implementadores, desarrolladores tecnológicos y otras partes interesadas en la salud digital. Organiza las intervenciones de salud digital en torno a capacidades tecnológicas específicas diseñadas para abordar desafíos de los sistemas de salud y las vincula con los servicios digitales y los tipos de aplicaciones mediante los cuales se prestan. La publicación actualiza y amplía la primera edición, publicada en 2018, para reflejar los avances en las tecnologías de salud digital, la evolución de las prácticas de implementación y las lecciones aprendidas a partir de su utilización a nivel mundial. El marco se estructura en torno a tres ejes interrelacionados: los desafíos de los sistemas de salud, las intervenciones de salud digital y los tipos de servicios y aplicaciones digitales. Incluye intervenciones dirigidas a las personas, los proveedores de atención sanitaria, los gestores de sistemas de salud y los servicios de datos, junto con categorías de aplicaciones digitales y sistemas de información. La clasificación está concebida para apoyar la planificación, la implementación, el análisis de inversiones, la investigación, las consideraciones de interoperabilidad, la elaboración de políticas y la gobernanza de las iniciativas de salud digital, facilitando así un uso más coherente y eficaz de las tecnologías digitales en los sistemas de salud. f838abb0908a.doc: Guidelines on long-acting injectable cabotegravir for HIV prevention
f838abb0908a.title: Guidelines on long-acting injectable cabotegravir for HIV prevention
f838abb0908a.content: World Health Organization (2022). Guidelines on long-acting injectable cabotegravir for HIV prevention. World Health Organization. TitleGuidelines on long-acting injectable cabotegravir for HIV prevention AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2022-7-27 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240054097 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis guideline provides evidence-informed recommendations on the use of long-acting injectable cabotegravir (CAB-LA) as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for HIV prevention in people at substantial risk of HIV infection. Developed according to WHO guideline development procedures, it is based on systematic reviews, GRADE assessments and additional evidence on effectiveness, safety, acceptability, feasibility, equity and cost–effectiveness. The document reviews the global HIV prevention context, the rationale for expanding HIV prevention choices, and the evidence supporting CAB-LA as an additional PrEP option. It also outlines the principles guiding implementation within a public health and human rights framework and identifies the intended audiences for the recommendations. The guideline recommends that long-acting injectable cabotegravir may be offered as an additional HIV prevention choice as part of combination prevention approaches for people at substantial risk of HIV infection. It discusses key implementation considerations, including HIV testing, service delivery models, comprehensive prevention services, community engagement, provider training and adherence support. The publication also identifies priority research gaps related to safety, drug resistance, delivery strategies and population-level impact, and describes the guideline development process, dissemination strategy and supporting evidence underpinning the recommendation. c45929eeac3a.content: World Health Organization (2018). Classification of digital health interventions v1.0: a shared language to describe the uses of digital technology for health. World Health Organization. TitleClassification of digital health interventions v1.0: a shared language to describe the uses of digital technology for health AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2018-3-14 Typereport PublisherWorld Health Organization Languageen AbstractThis publication presents version 1.0 of the World Health Organization’s Classification of Digital Health Interventions (DHIs), a taxonomy developed to provide a shared and standardized language for describing how digital and mobile technologies are used to address health system needs. Intended primarily for public health audiences, the framework supports communication among policymakers, programme planners, implementers, researchers, donors and technology specialists by defining digital health interventions as discrete digital functionalities linked to specific health objectives. The classification was developed to facilitate evidence synthesis, landscape analyses, planning processes and the articulation of digital solutions to identified health system challenges. The framework organizes digital health interventions into four primary groups according to the main user: clients, health-care providers, health system managers and data services. It links digital interventions to broader health system challenges and to system categories such as electronic medical records, logistics management information systems and telemedicine platforms. Developed through technical consultations, literature review and public feedback, the classification builds on existing mHealth and eHealth frameworks while providing a simplified and practical reference for health programmes. The document is intended to support the design, implementation, evaluation and interoperability of digital health initiatives and will be periodically updated to reflect emerging technologies and evolving practices in digital health. TitleNational health workforce accounts: a handbook AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2023-11-23 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240081291 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThe National Health Workforce Accounts (NHWA) Handbook, second edition, provides the conceptual framework, standards, methods and indicators that support the systematic collection, analysis and use of health workforce data for evidence-informed policy-making and planning. Developed by the World Health Organization, the handbook supports implementation of the National Health Workforce Accounts as a country-led system to strengthen human resources for health information systems, improve data quality and availability, and monitor progress towards universal health coverage, the Sustainable Development Goals and other global health objectives. It describes the rationale, principles and applications of NHWA at national, regional and global levels and outlines a modular approach to health workforce monitoring. The handbook presents guidance on implementation and reporting methods and defines a set of standardized indicators organized into four modules covering workforce stock and flows, education, finance and expenditures, and working conditions, governance and leadership. It explains indicator metadata, calculation methods, disaggregation requirements and reporting standards, and illustrates how NHWA data can be used to support workforce planning, policy development, retention strategies, equity analyses and monitoring of health workforce trends. The revised edition incorporates updated indicators, occupational classifications, tools and guidance to address evolving health workforce priorities and emerging global health challenges. 604838e76baf.content: World Health Organization (2024). Digital transformation handbook for primary health care: optimizing person-centred point of service systems. World Health Organization. TitleDigital transformation handbook for primary health care: optimizing person-centred point of service systems AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2024-11-4 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240093362 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis handbook provides practical guidance for countries seeking to digitally transform primary health care through the development and implementation of person-centred point of service systems (PCPOSS). It addresses the transition from paper-based and fragmented digital systems towards integrated, interoperable digital solutions that support service delivery, continuity of care, data use and health system strengthening. Grounded in WHO recommendations on digital interventions for health system strengthening and aligned with the SMART Guidelines framework, the publication outlines approaches for translating clinical and public health guidance into digital systems while maintaining fidelity to normative standards. The publication presents a stepwise methodology covering assessment of digital readiness, identification of user requirements, workflow and business process mapping, system design and adaptation, software selection, testing, deployment and scale-up. It emphasizes person-centred care, interoperability, longitudinal health records, decision support and the use of standards-based digital architectures. Through practical tools, worksheets and implementation guidance, the publication supports policy-makers, programme managers, digital health practitioners and software developers in designing and optimizing digital systems that improve service quality, strengthen accountability and enable more effective, integrated and responsive primary health care services. 6f11d082015d.content: Lundgren, Jens D; Raben, Dorthe; Ерамова, Ирина; et al. (2014). Лечение и уход в связи с ВИЧ/СПИДом в Беларуси: отчет оценочной миссии: январь 2014 г.. Всемирная организация здравоохранения. Европейское региональное бюро. TitleЛечение и уход в связи с ВИЧ/СПИДом в Беларуси: отчет оценочной миссии: январь 2014 г. AuthorsLundgren, Jens D; Raben, Dorthe; Ерамова, Ирина; Ильенкова, Вера Issued2014-12-31 Typereport PublisherВсемирная организация здравоохранения. Европейское региональное бюро Languageru AbstractОценка лечения и ухода в связи с ВИЧ/СПИДом выполнена с учетом стратегии или концепции ВОЗ/ЮНЭЙДС «Лечение 2.0», где указаны пять приоритетных областей: оптимизация лекарственных схем, обеспечение доступа к диагностике в местах оказания помощи, снижение стоимости, адаптация систем оказания услуг и мобилизация сообществ или гражданского общества. Для оценки использованы результаты анализа существующих документов и отчетов и страновой миссии, которая состоялась 11-14 ноября 2013 года в гор. Минске и Солигорске, Беларусь. Особое внимание было уделено практике тестирования на ВИЧ, поскольку именно здесь начинается лечение и уход в связи с ВИЧ, а также уязвимым группам и обеспечению доступа к лечению и уходу. Кроме того, была проанализирована устойчивость программ в свете используемых в настоящее время и будущих международных и национальных схем финансирования. a1db7f19a935.title: Estrategia mundial sobre salud digital 2020–2025
a1db7f19a935.content: Organización Mundial de la Salud (2021). Estrategia mundial sobre salud digital 2020–2025. Organización Mundial de la Salud. TitleEstrategia mundial sobre salud digital 2020–2025 AuthorsOrganización Mundial de la Salud Issued2021-8-18 Typebook PublisherOrganización Mundial de la Salud ISBN9789240027572 (versión electrónica) Languagees AbstractLa Estrategia mundial sobre salud digital 2020–2025 proporciona un marco para apoyar a los Estados Miembros en el fortalecimiento de los sistemas de salud mediante la adopción y el uso adecuados de las tecnologías digitales. Elaborada en respuesta a los mandatos de la Asamblea Mundial de la Salud y alineada con los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible y las metas de los “Tres Mil Millones” de la OMS, la estrategia establece una visión compartida para mejorar la salud y el bienestar a través de soluciones de salud digital accesibles, asequibles, seguras y sostenibles. Destaca la importancia de una gobernanza sólida, la interoperabilidad, el uso ético de los datos, la protección de la privacidad, el fortalecimiento de las capacidades del personal sanitario y la inversión en infraestructura digital para apoyar las prioridades nacionales de salud y la cobertura sanitaria universal. El documento define cuatro objetivos estratégicos: promover la colaboración mundial y el intercambio de conocimientos; avanzar en la implementación de estrategias nacionales de salud digital; fortalecer la gobernanza de la salud digital a nivel mundial, regional y nacional; y fomentar sistemas de salud centrados en las personas mediante el uso de tecnologías digitales. Asimismo, presenta principios rectores, un marco de implementación y mecanismos de seguimiento destinados a apoyar a los países en el desarrollo de ecosistemas de salud digital interoperables. Se presta especial atención a los obstáculos que enfrentan los países de ingresos bajos y medianos y a garantizar que la transformación digital contribuya a sistemas de salud más equitativos, eficaces y resilientes. Zhang, Chi. What Keeps Agent Skills from Being Reusable? Evidence from 138K SKILL.md Files. TitleWhat Keeps Agent Skills from Being Reusable? Evidence from 138K SKILL.md Files AuthorsZhang, Chi IssuedD:20260811 Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2608.08453 AbstractUnder the current standard, Agent Skills are SKILL.md files that combine instructions with supporting resources, en- abling Large Language Model (LLM) agents to reuse proce- dures beyond a single conversation. Yet many public skills appear to originate from a single task, repository, or conver- sation, even when they are shared as reusable components. We analyze this gap across 138,133 public SKILL.md files from 20,556 repositories using a two-tier defect taxonomy grounded in the official specification and best-practice guid- ance. We find that 91.8% of skills contain at least one de- tected defect, with stable estimates across lenient and strict thresholds (88.8–94.6%). The dominant failures are ordinary packaging problems rather than exotic attacks: weak routing metadata, bloated or non-actionable bodies, and poor re- source organization. A deterministic routing stress test over 20,000 skills shows the functional impact: skills with valid routing metadata are retrieved more reliably from startup descriptions than skills with routing defects. Defect rates vary by platform and provenance: specification-aware skills contain fewer defects, while AI-marked skills show more safety and portability problems. Lightweight enforcement and repair experiments support a quality-assured generation workflow combining spec-aware prompting, lightweight lint- ing, automated repair, and safety gating. Son, Seongho; Yoon, Sangwoong; Tang, Jiahua; et al.. SWE-Router: Routing in Multi-turn Agentic Software Engineering Tasks. TitleSWE-Router: Routing in Multi-turn Agentic Software Engineering Tasks AuthorsSon, Seongho; Yoon, Sangwoong; Tang, Jiahua; Wang, Shuhan; Wolf, Lorenz; Bogunovic, Ilija Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2607.00053 AbstractLarge language models (LLMs) embedded in multi-turn agentic harnesses are reshaping soft- ware engineering (SWE), but routing every task to a frontier model is wasteful when many issues admit cheap fixes. Existing LLM routers operate on the task description alone, which inherits an information-theoretic Bayes-error floor in agentic settings: a similar issue can hide either a localized typo or a multi-module refactor, and the prompt does not separate the two. We introduce SWE- Router, a value-based temporal approach that lets a cheap model run for a few exploratory turns and reads the resulting partial trajectory before de- ciding whether to continue cheaply or to escalate to an expensive model. We provide a Bayes- optimality theorem showing that conditioning on the partial trajectory never harms routing and is strictly better whenever exploration is informative. Across the LLM pairs of weak and strong models spanning the contemporary cost–capability frontier, we show that SWE-Router greatly improves the cost efficiency of SWE tasks, while maintaining the majority of the performances of the stronger model. We additionally release a multi-LLM trajectory dataset which allows reproduction of our trajectory-level routing. Sources . | arxiv.org/abs/2607.00053 (canonical) | . Rawal, Kaivalya. Evaluating Model Explanations without Ground Truth. TitleEvaluating Model Explanations without Ground Truth AuthorsRawal, Kaivalya IssuedD:20250611 Typearticle-journal DOI10.1145/3715275.3732219 NotearXiv:2505.10399 AbstractThere can be many competing and contradictory explanations for a single model prediction, making it difficult to select which one to use. Current explanation evaluation frameworks measure qual- ity by comparing against ideal “ground-truth” explanations, or by verifying model sensitivity to important inputs. We outline the limitations of these approaches, and propose three desirable princi- ples to ground the future development of explanation evaluation strategies for local feature importance explanations. We propose a ground-truth Agnostic eXplanation Evaluation framework (AXE) for evaluating and comparing model explanations that satis- fies these principles. Unlike prior approaches, AXE does not require access to ideal ground-truth explanations for comparison, or rely on model sensitivity – providing an independent measure of expla- nation quality. We verify AXE by comparing with baselines, and show how it can be used to detect explanation fairwashing. Our code is available at https://github.com/KaiRawal/Evaluating-Model- Explanations-without-Ground-Truth. CCS Concepts • Computing methodologies →Artificial intelligence; Ma- chine learning. Harris1, Joshua; †; Laurence1, Timothy; et al.. Evaluating Large Language Models for Public Health Classification and Extraction Tasks. TitleEvaluating Large Language Models for Public Health Classification and Extraction Tasks AuthorsHarris1, Joshua; †; Laurence1, Timothy; Loman1, Leo; Grayson1, Fan; Nonnenmacher1, Toby; Harry IssuedD:20250220 Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2405.14766 AbstractAdvances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have led to significant interest in their potential to support human experts across a range of domains, including public health. In this work we present automated evaluations of LLMs for public health tasks involving the classification and extraction of free text. We combine six externally annotated datasets with seven new internally annotated datasets to evaluate LLMs for processing text related to: health burden, epidemiological risk factors, and public health interventions. We evaluate eleven open-weight LLMs (7-123 billion parameters) across all tasks using zero-shot in-context learning. We find that Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct is the highest performing model, achieving the best results on 8/16 tasks (using micro-F1 scores). We see significant variation across tasks with all open-weight LLMs scoring below 60% micro-F1 on some challenging tasks, such as Contact Classification, while all LLMs achieve greater than 80% micro-F1 on others, such as GI Illness Classification. For a subset of 11 tasks, we also evaluate three GPT-4 and GPT-4o series models and find comparable results to Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct. Overall, based on these initial results we find promising signs that LLMs may be useful tools for public health experts to extract information from a wide variety of free text sources, and support public health surveillance, research, and interventions. Investigating the impact of representation features on decision model comprehension (Extended Abstract). TitleInvestigating the impact of representation features on decision model comprehension (Extended Abstract) IssuedD:20240502 Typearticle-journal DOI10.18420/EMISA2024_05 Abstract)5 Djordje Djurica 1, Tyge F. Kummer 2, Jan Mendling 1,3, and Kathrin Figl 4 Abstract: Decision models play a crucial role in the development of information systems for tasks such as system analysis and design, as well as compliance management. The effective presentation of these models is essential to ensure their accuracy and completeness. Existing research on their cognitive effectiveness remains inconclusive. Our study advances understanding by examining the detailed representation features of decision models, including type (tree versus table), structure (expanded versus frugal), and design (monochromatic versus colored). We demonstrate that the use of color can improve model-task fit, and that structural features can enhance comprehension. Utilizing eye-tracking, we analyzed the underlying mechanisms of these effects. Our findings provide valuable insights for cognitive information systems research and practical applications, offering guidance for both users and developers of decision models. Tang1, Xunzhu; Kim2, Kisub; Song1, Yewei; et al.. CodeAgent : Autonomous Communicative Agents for Code Review. TitleCodeAgent : Autonomous Communicative Agents for Code Review AuthorsTang1, Xunzhu; Kim2, Kisub; Song1, Yewei; Lothritz3, Cedric; Li4, Bei; Ezzini5, Saad IssuedD:20240926 Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2402.02172 AbstractCode review, which aims at ensuring the over- all quality and reliability of software, is a cor- nerstone of software development. Unfortu- nately, while crucial, Code review is a labor- intensive process that the research community is looking to automate. Existing automated methods rely on single input-output generative models and thus generally struggle to emulate the collaborative nature of code review. This work introduces CodeAgent, a novel multi- agent Large Language Model (LLM) system for code review automation. CodeAgent in- corporates a supervisory agent, QA-Checker, to ensure that all the agents’ contributions ad- dress the initial review question. We evaluated CodeAgent on critical code review tasks: (1) detect inconsistencies between code changes and commit messages, (2) identify vulnerabil- ity introductions, (3) validate code style ad- herence, and (4) suggest code revision. The results demonstrate CodeAgent’s effective- ness, contributing to a new state-of-the-art in code review automation. Our data and code are publicly available (https://github. com/Code4Agent/codeagent). Sources . | arxiv.org/abs/2402.02172 (canonical) | . Tekanlou1, Hadi Bayrami Asl; Razmara1, Jafar; Sanaei1, Mahsa. Homa at SemEval-2025 Task 5: Aligning Librarian Records with OntoAligner for Subject Tagging. TitleHoma at SemEval-2025 Task 5: Aligning Librarian Records with OntoAligner for Subject Tagging AuthorsTekanlou1, Hadi Bayrami Asl; Razmara1, Jafar; Sanaei1, Mahsa IssuedD:20250501 Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2504.21474 AbstractThis paper presents our system, Homa, for SemEval-2025 Task 5: Subject Tagging, which focuses on automatically assigning subject la- bels to technical records from TIBKAT us- ing the Gemeinsame Normdatei (GND) tax- onomy. We leverage OntoAligner, a modu- lar ontology alignment toolkit, to address this task by integrating retrieval-augmented genera- tion (RAG) techniques. Our approach formu- lates the subject tagging problem as an align- ment task, where records are matched to GND categories based on semantic similarity. We evaluate OntoAligner’s adaptability for sub- ject indexing and analyze its effectiveness in handling multilingual records. Experimental results demonstrate the strengths and limita- tions of this method, highlighting the potential of alignment techniques for improving subject tagging in digital libraries. Institute for Parallel; Systems, Distributed. AI-assisted JSON Schema Creation and Mapping. TitleAI-assisted JSON Schema Creation and Mapping AuthorsInstitute for Parallel; Systems, Distributed Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2508.05192 AbstractModel-Driven Engineering (MDE) places models at the core of system and data engineering processes. In the context of research data, these models are typically expressed as schemas that define the structure and semantics of datasets. However, many domains still lack standardized models, and creating them remains a significant barrier, especially for non- experts. We present a hybrid approach that combines large language models (LLMs) with deterministic techniques to enable JSON Schema creation, modification, and schema mapping based on natural language inputs by the user. These capabilities are integrated into the open-source tool MetaConfigurator, which already provides visual model editing, validation, code gener- ation, and form generation from models. For data integration, we generate schema mappings from heterogeneous JSON, CSV, XML, and YAML data using LLMs, while ensuring scalability and reliability through deterministic execution of generated mapping rules. The applicability of our work is demonstrated in an application example in the field of chemistry. By combining natural language interaction with deterministic safeguards, this work significantly lowers the barrier to structured data modeling and data integration for non-experts. Li†, Han. SWE-Debate: Competitive Multi-Agent Debate for Software Issue Resolution. TitleSWE-Debate: Competitive Multi-Agent Debate for Software Issue Resolution AuthorsLi†, Han IssuedD:20250801 Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2507.23348 AbstractIssue resolution has made remarkable progress thanks to the ad- vanced reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs). Recently, agent-based frameworks such as SWE-agent have further advanced this progress by enabling autonomous, tool-using agents to tackle complex software engineering tasks. While existing agent- based issue resolution approaches are primarily based on agents’ independent explorations, they often get stuck in local solutions and fail to identify issue patterns that span across different parts of the codebase. To address this limitation, we propose SWE-Debate, a competitive multi-agent debate framework that encourages diverse reasoning paths and achieves more consolidated issue localization. SWE-Debate first creates multiple fault propagation traces as local- ization proposals by traversing a code dependency graph. Then, it organizes a three-round debate among specialized agents, each em- bodying distinct reasoning perspectives along the fault propagation trace. This structured competition enables agents to collaboratively converge on a consolidated fix plan. Finally, this consolidated fix plan is integrated into an MCTS-based code modification agent for patch generation. Experiments on the SWE-bench benchmark show that SWE-Debate achieves new state-of-the-art results in open-source agent frameworks and outperforms baselines by a large margin1. Destefanis, Giuseppe. Authoring Agent Skills: A Software-Engineering Approach. TitleAuthoring Agent Skills: A Software-Engineering Approach AuthorsDestefanis, Giuseppe Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2607.25032 AbstractAgent Skills are an emerging way to extend large language model agents with reusable procedural knowledge that the agent loads on demand. Anthropic introduced Agent Skills and published the format as an open specification supported across several agent tools. This note argues that a skill is a software artefact and that its construction should follow software-engineering principles, with qualifications: single responsibility, separation of interface from implementation, low coupling, and economy in a shared token budget, together with behavioural evaluation in place of deterministic testing. Using Claude Code as the reference implementation, it describes how a skill is structured, how its contents are loaded in stages, and how to write the description on which selection depends. It places skills against the other mechanisms a developer can use to shape agent behaviour, like project memory files, slash commands, subagents, external tool connections, and hooks, and gives a rule for choosing between them based on who decides that a mechanism runs and what guarantee it provides. It then sets out an evaluation-driven authoring process, a set of patterns and faults commonly encountered in authoring, and the trust question raised by using skills from third parties. We illustrate the comparison drawn in UML class style, the loading model, the anatomy of a skill, the relative position of each mechanism, and the points at which skills and hooks act during a session. Note on sources This note draws on Anthropic’s official documentation1 for Agent Skills, Claude Code skills, hooks, and skill authoring best practices, together with the open Agent Skills specification. Iannella, Renato; Monegraph; r@iannel.la. ODRL Information Model 2.2. TitleODRL Information Model 2.2 AuthorsIannella, Renato; Monegraph; r@iannel.la IssuedD:20261001 Typedocument AbstractThe Open Digital Rights Language (ODRL) is a policy expression language that provides a flexible and interoperable information model, vocabulary, and encoding mechanisms for representing statements about the usage of content and services. The ODRL Information Model describes the underlying concepts, entities, and relationships that form the foundational basis for the semantics of the ODRL policies. Policies are used to represent permitted and prohibited actions over a certain asset, as well as the obligations required to be meet by stakeholders. In addition, policies may be limited by constraints (e.g., temporal or spatial constraints) and duties (e.g. payments) may be imposed on permissions. Chow, Eric H. C.. A Skill-Based Agentic Pipeline for Library of Congress Subject Indexing. TitleA Skill-Based Agentic Pipeline for Library of Congress Subject Indexing AuthorsChow, Eric H. C. Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2605.03537 AbstractThis paper presents a modular AI agentic skill pipeline for au- tomating subject indexing with Library of Congress Subject Headings (LCSH). Subject indexing—the process of analyzing a work’s aboutness, selecting controlled vocabulary terms, and encoding them as MARC 21 subject access fields—is one of the most time-consuming components of library cataloging. The system decomposes this process into four discrete, sequentially executed agent skills: conceptual analysis, quantitative filtering, authority validation, and MARC field synthesis. Each skill encodes domain knowledge drawn directly from Library of Congress Subject Headings Manual (SHM) instruction sheets and subject analysis theory. The pipeline was evaluated against a corpus of ten titles whose existing subject headings were captured from the Harvard Library bibliographic dataset (a snapshot of their Alma ILS). Results demonstrate strong con- ceptual alignment with professional subject indexing practice, with notable differences in specificity, subdivision practice, and the agent’s adherence to the 2026 LC policy discontinuing form subdivisions ($v) in favor of LCGFT 655 fields. MEASURES, IT. The Metanym Game: An LLM Benchmark Without Ground Truth That Rises With the Models It Measures. TitleThe Metanym Game: An LLM Benchmark Without Ground Truth That Rises With the Models It Measures AuthorsMEASURES, IT Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2606.21008 AbstractWe introduce a benchmark that is fully self-contained, needs no ground truth, and rises with the models it measures. Language models compete at making analo- gies and subjectively grade one another; nothing enters from outside. The bench- mark reproduces GPQA Diamond, a keyed benchmark of expert-written ques- tions, at r = 0.98, audited for a leak and found clean. We hypothesize that both benchmarks measure the same thing in different ways: a language model holds its knowledge as archetypal contexts, relationship patterns valid across many topic domains. GPQA instantiates the required knowledge in one domain; the Metanym Game instantiates one archetype into several domains, generating analogies, no reasoning required. The reasoning feature of an LLM hardly changes the game’s ratings, while it lifts GPQA, which requires derivations. In the game, a player writes a context template whose slots, filled with a set of keywords from a topic domain, instantiate a factually true description of that domain; the instantiations are each other’s metaphors, and keywords filling the same slot are metanyms, metaphorically synonymous. Correctness is settled sentence by sentence. Ground truth is replaced by the SVD of the factual rating matrix: its left and right singular vectors rate the players as judges and as generators, two ratings from one factori- sation, to our knowledge a first for an LLM council of peers. On the subjective criteria, judges are weighted by their rating consistency under a swept calibration anchor. Generating and judging are different skills: on this roster the strongest generators were middling judges. A council of the five best issues the official ratings; its contestable seats keep it current, a candidate steering signal for self- improving AI. The paper is accompanied by a validating package that recomputes every number. Sources . | arxiv.org/abs/2606.21008 (canonical) | . Calvanese1, Diego; Dumas2, Marlon; Laurson2, Ülari. Semantics and Analysis of DMN Decision Tables. TitleSemantics and Analysis of DMN Decision Tables AuthorsCalvanese1, Diego; Dumas2, Marlon; Laurson2, Ülari IssuedD:20160325 Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:1603.07466 AbstractThe Decision Model and Notation (DMN) is a standard no- tation to capture decision logic in business applications in general and business processes in particular. A central construct in DMN is that of a decision table. The increasing use of DMN decision tables to capture critical business knowledge raises the need to support analysis tasks on these tables such as correctness and completeness checking. This paper provides a formal semantics for DMN tables, a formal deﬁnition of key analysis tasks and scalable algorithms to tackle two such tasks, i.e., de- tection of overlapping rules and of missing rules. The algorithms are based on a geometric interpretation of decision tables that can be used to support other analysis tasks by tapping into geometric algorithms. The algorithms have been implemented in an open-source DMN editor and tested on large decision tables derived from a credit lending dataset. Sources . | arxiv.org/abs/1603.07466 (canonical) | . [0000-0002-4210-2342], Ed Overes1; Santoro2[0000-0003-3421-1894], Flavia Maria. The Effectiveness of Business Process Visualisations: a Systematic Literature Review. TitleThe Effectiveness of Business Process Visualisations: a Systematic Literature Review Authors[0000-0002-4210-2342], Ed Overes1; Santoro2[0000-0003-3421-1894], Flavia Maria IssuedD:20250415 Typedocument AbstractBusiness Process Visualisations (BPVs) have become indispensable tools for organisations seeking to enhance their operational efficiency, decision-making capabilities, and overall performance. The burgeoning interest in process modeling and tool development, coupled with the rise of data visualisation field, underscores the significant role of visual tools in leveraging human cognition. Unlike traditional models, data visualisation approaches graphics from a novel angle, emphasising the potency of visual representations. This review aims to integrate the domains of BPV and data visualisation to assess their combined influence on organisational effectiveness comprehensively. Through a meticulous analysis of existing literature, this study aims to amalgamate insights on BPVs impact from a data visualisation standpoint, advocating for a design philosophy that prioritises user engagement to bolster organisational outcomes. Additionally, our systematic review has unveiled promising avenues for future research, identifying underexplored variables that influence the efficacy of BPVs, thereby charting a path for forthcoming scholarly inquiries. TitlePROV-O: The PROV Ontology AuthorsTimothy Lebo, Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, USA IssuedD:20261001 Typedocument AbstractThe PROV Ontology (PROV-O) expresses the PROV Data Model [PROV-DM] using the OWL2 Web Ontology Language (OWL2) [OWL2- OVERVIEW]. It provides a set of classes, properties, and restrictions that can be used to represent and interchange provenance information generated in different systems and under different contexts. It can also be specialized to create new classes and properties to model provenance information for different applications and domains. The PROV Document Overview describes the overall state of PROV, and should be read before other PROV documents. The namespace for all PROV-O terms is http://www.w3.org/ns/prov#. The OWL encoding of the PROV Ontology is available here. Status of This Document This section describes the status of this document at the time of its publication. Chen, Sizhe. Defending Against Prompt Injection With a Few DefensiveTokens. TitleDefending Against Prompt Injection With a Few DefensiveTokens AuthorsChen, Sizhe IssuedD:20250826 Typearticle-journal DOI10.1145/3733799.3762982 NotearXiv:2507.07974 AbstractWhen large language model (LLM) systems interact with exter- nal data to perform complex tasks, a new attack, namely prompt injection, becomes a significant threat. By injecting instructions into the data accessed by the system, the attacker is able to over- ride the initial user task with an arbitrary task directed by the attacker. To secure the system, test-time defenses, e.g., defensive prompting, have been proposed for system developers to attain security only when needed in a flexible manner. However, they are much less effective than training-time defenses that change the model parameters. Motivated by this, we propose DefensiveToken, a test-time defense with prompt injection robustness comparable to training-time alternatives. DefensiveTokens are newly inserted as special tokens, whose embeddings are optimized for security. In security-sensitive cases, system developers can append a few DefensiveTokens before the LLM input to achieve security with a minimal utility drop. In scenarios where security is less of a con- cern, developers can simply skip DefensiveTokens; the LLM system remains the same as there is no defense, generating high-quality responses. Thus, DefensiveTokens, if released alongside the model, allow a flexible switch between the state-of-the-art (SOTA) utility and almost-SOTA security at test time. The code is available here. Annif at SemEval-2025 Task 5: Traditional XMTC augmented by LLMs. TitleAnnif at SemEval-2025 Task 5: Traditional XMTC augmented by LLMs AuthorsSuominen, Osma; Inkinen, Juho; Lehtinen, Mona Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2504.19675 AbstractThis paper presents the Annif system in SemEval-2025 Task 5 (LLMs4Subjects), which focussed on subject indexing using large lan- guage models (LLMs). The task required creating subject predictions for bibliographic records from the bilingual TIBKAT database using the GND subject vocabulary. Our ap- proach combines traditional natural language processing and machine learning techniques im- plemented in the Annif toolkit with innovative LLM-based methods for translation and syn- thetic data generation, and merging predictions from monolingual models. The system ranked first in the all-subjects category and second in the tib-core-subjects category in the quantita- tive evaluation, and fourth in qualitative evalu- ations. These findings demonstrate the poten- tial of combining traditional XMTC algorithms with modern LLM techniques to improve the accuracy and efficiency of subject indexing in multilingual contexts. Wang1, Yizhu; Chen1, Sizhe; Alkhudair2, Raghad; et al.. Defending Against Prompt Injection with DataFilter. TitleDefending Against Prompt Injection with DataFilter AuthorsWang1, Yizhu; Chen1, Sizhe; Alkhudair2, Raghad; Alomair2, Basel; Wagner1, David Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2510.19207 AbstractWhen large language model (LLM) agents are in- creasingly deployed to automate tasks and interact with untrusted external data, prompt injection emerges as a significant security threat. By injecting malicious instructions into the data that LLMs access, an attacker can arbitrarily override the original user task and redirect the agent toward unintended, potentially harmful actions. Existing defenses either require access to model weights (fine-tuning), incur substantial utility loss (detection- based), or demand non-trivial system redesign (system-level). Motivated by this, we propose DataFilter, a test-time model- agnostic defense that removes malicious instructions from the data before it reaches the backend LLM. DataFilter is trained with supervised fine-tuning on simulated injections and leverages both the user’s instruction and the data to selectively strip adversarial content while preserving benign information. Across multiple benchmarks, DataFilter consistently reduces the prompt injection attack success rates to near zero while maintaining the LLMs’ utility. DataFilter delivers strong security, high utility, and plug-and-play deployment, making it a strong practical defense to secure black-box commercial LLMs against prompt injection. Our DataFilter model is released here for immediate use, with the code to reproduce our results here. 1 Index Terms—Large Language Models (LLMs), Prompt Injec- tion, Data Filtering, LLM Security I. INTRODUCTION AI agents [1, 2] have automated diverse tasks like web- navigation and tool-calling. In agents, the Large Language Model (LLM) interacts with the external environment (web- sites, documents, emails, etc.), where the data is untrusted and may contain a prompt injection attack [3, 4]. By injecting a prompt into the data that LLMs access, an attacker can arbitrarily override the original user task and redirect the agent system towards unintended and potentially harmful actions. c88ae04d1aa9.content: The reference for cat-harness/library/corpus/kg/arxiv-2202.02427v1 (cat-harness, a dependency of smart-trust) and any references extracted from it. cat-harness-library · All references. Hang1, Mengyue; Schnabel2, Tobias; Yang2, Longqi; et al.. Lightweight Compositional Embeddings for Incremental Streaming Recommendation. TitleLightweight Compositional Embeddings for Incremental Streaming Recommendation AuthorsHang1, Mengyue; Schnabel2, Tobias; Yang2, Longqi; Neville1, Jennifer; 2 IssuedD:20220208 Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2202.02427 AbstractMost work in graph-based recommender systems considers a static setting where all information about test nodes (i.e., users and items) is available upfront at training time. However, this static setting makes little sense for many real world applications where data comes in continuously as a stream of new edges and nodes, and one has to update model predictions incrementally to reflect the latest state. To fully capitalize on the newly available data in the stream, recent graph-based recommendation models would need to be repeatedly retrained, which is infeasible in practice. In this pa- per, we study the graph-based streaming recommendation setting and propose a compositional recommendation model—Lightweight Compositional Embedding (LCE)—that supports incremental up- dates under low computational cost. Instead of learning explicit embeddings for the full set of nodes, LCE learns explicit embed- dings for only a subset of nodes and represents the other nodes implicitly, through a composition function based on their interac- tions in the graph. This provides an effective, yet efficient, means to leverage streaming graph data when one node type (e.g., items) is more amenable to static representation. We conduct an extensive empirical study to compare LCE to a set of competitive baselines on three large-scale user-item recommendation datasets with inter- actions under a streaming setting. The results demonstrate the su- perior performance of LCE, showing that it achieves nearly skyline performance with significantly fewer parameters than alternative graph-based models. Yan Liua, b; Jhaa, Abhinav K.; b. How accurately can quantitative imaging methods be ranked without ground truth: An upper bound on no-gold-standard evaluation. TitleHow accurately can quantitative imaging methods be ranked without ground truth: An upper bound on no-gold-standard evaluation AuthorsYan Liua, b; Jhaa, Abhinav K.; b IssuedD:20240326 Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2403.16873 AbstractObjective evaluation of quantitative imaging (QI) methods with patient data, while important, is typically hindered by the lack of gold standards. To address this challenge, no-gold-standard evaluation (NGSE) techniques have been proposed. These techniques have demonstrated efficacy in accurately ranking QI methods without access to gold standards. The development of NGSE methods has raised an important question: how accurately can QI methods be ranked without ground truth. To answer this question, we propose a Cram´er–Rao bound (CRB)-based framework that quantifies the upper bound in ranking QI methods without any ground truth. We present the application of this framework in guiding the use of a well-known NGSE technique, namely the regression-without-truth (RWT) technique. Our results show the utility of this framework in quantifying the performance of this NGSE technique for different patient numbers. These results provide motivation towards studying other applications of this upper bound. Sources . | arxiv.org/abs/2403.16873 (canonical) | . a10cd66e1c2e.content: The reference for cat-harness/library/corpus/content/arxiv-2505.06046v4 (cat-harness, a dependency of smart-trust) and any references extracted from it. cat-harness-library · All references. KNOWL-, BENCHMARKING LLM. Healthy LLMs? Benchmarking LLM Knowledge of UK Government Public Health Information. TitleHealthy LLMs? Benchmarking LLM Knowledge of UK Government Public Health Information AuthorsKNOWL-, BENCHMARKING LLM Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2505.06046 AbstractAs Large Language Models (LLMs) become widely accessible, a detailed un- derstanding of their knowledge within specific domains becomes necessary for successful real world use. This is particularly critical in the domains of medicine and public health, where failure to retrieve relevant, accurate, and current infor- mation could significantly impact UK residents. However, while there are a num- ber of LLM benchmarks in the medical domain, currently little is known about LLM knowledge within the field of public health. To address this issue, this pa- per introduces a new benchmark, PubHealthBench, with over 8000 questions for evaluating LLMs’ Multiple Choice Question Answering (MCQA) and free form responses to public health queries. To create PubHealthBench we extract free text from 687 current UK government guidance documents and implement an automated pipeline for generating MCQA samples. Assessing 24 LLMs on Pub- HealthBench we find the latest proprietary LLMs (GPT-4.5, GPT-4.1 and o1) have a high degree of knowledge, achieving over 90% accuracy in the MCQA setup, and outperform humans with cursory search engine use. However, in the free form setup we see lower performance with no model scoring over 75%. There- fore, while there are promising signs that state of the art (SOTA) LLMs are an increasingly accurate source of public health information, additional safeguards or tools may still be needed when providing free form responses.
